text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The National Oil Company said refineries were faced with an acute crude oil shortage. It said the oil they had was enough to last one more day of operation.
- The Bucharest commodities exchange will organise a tender on Thursday to sell 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron.
ADEVARUL
- Medicine prices will go up as pharmaceuticals factories were allowed to reassess production prices in line with a depreciated leu.
TINERETUL LIBER
- The Bucharest stock exchange management are analysing files from 34 companies which applied for a listing.
ZIUA
- Romania is affected by an acute petrol shortage which has swollen queues at filling stations.
- Zephir, one of the bidders in the tender for a GSM licence in Romania, sued the Communications Ministry demanding an annulment of tender results.
LIBERTATEA
- Creditors of troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA meet in Transylvanian city of Cluj on Tuesday hoping to take one more step towards the bank's recovery.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Romania and Bulgaria have resumed talks on the building of a bridge across the Danube.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The newspaper's editorial slams the lower Chamber of Deputies' intention to set its headquarters in Ceausescu's palace -- which cost hundreds of billions of lei to furnish -- while newly-elected politicians speak of "austerity measures".
- MPs have to deposit a statement on their wealth prior to being validated. The statements come in sealed envelopes and can be opened only if someone questions the means of acquiring that wealth.
ADEVARUL
- Police released Syrian Zaher Iskandarani pending a trial on alleged charges of tax evasion worth some 41 billion lei in coffee and cigarettes smuggling.

- A former intelligence officer is charged with breaking the national security law after revealing alleged illegal phonetaps by the Romanian Intelligence Service. He will be tried by a military court.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Interior Minister will set up railway geandarmes corps to prevent the destruction of rolling stock, as well as violence on trains.
- The Democratic Convention, the Social Democratic Union and the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) are expected to sign a political accord to support the coalition government.

- Leaders of the Socialist Labour Party (PSM) discussed future cooperation with leaders of Greater Romania Party and the outgoing Party of Social Democracy in order to set up the "united left", PSM president Ilie Verdet said.
- Prime Minister designate Victor Ciorbea is expected to present a cabinet list and a governing programme before parliament next Thursday, the newspaper says.
- The UDMR is expected to get the jobs of local prefects for the Caras-Severin and Satu-Mare counties but not in the Covasna and Harghita counties where ethnic Hungarians make up the vast majority.
LIBERTATEA
- Health became a luxury for Romanians after medicine prices had risen by 50 percent.
- President-elect Emil Constantinescu said he would keep the presidency headquarters in its current building -- the Cotroceni Palace -- because moving would cost too much.

- Iskandarani will not leave Romania, but will continue to do business here, pledging to create 4,600 new jobs, his lawyer, Ioan Mustata said. Iskandarani pleaded not guilty in its file on alleged tax evasion.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Constantinescu is attending a seminar on supporting Romania's economy held in Munich.
- More than 100 hepatitis B cases were registered in northern town of Suceava in November.
AZI
- CDR senator Varujan Vosganian said a commission should be set up to evaluate the real economic situation the leftist government of Premier Nicolae Vacaroiu is leaving behind.
VOCEA ROMANIEI

- Results of Romania's general and presidential elections could lead to an increase in U.S. investments, U.S. ambassador to Romania Alfred Moses says in interview. ($=3,531 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
